transcript.text: Bosch PIE631BB5E hob switched one zone off and shows F2 while I was batch cooking on all four rings. What does F2 mean?

On Bosch hobs, F2 means the electronics underneath have overheated, so the hob has cut power to protect itself. It's a safety cut-out rather than a fault in its own right, and with all four rings going hard for a batch cook, overheating is the most likely explanation. Hobs with a PIE model prefix are typically induction. The power electronics on induction hobs make a lot of heat and rely on a fan and clear airflow underneath to stay cool. The likely causes, most likely first:
1. Simple heavy use. Several zones at high power (or boost) for a long time can push the electronics past their limit, especially in a warm kitchen.
2. Restricted airflow under the hob. This could be stuff packed into a drawer right under it, a blocked ventilation gap, or an oven below running at the same time and heating the space.
3. Less likely, the cooling fan isn't running properly, or a temperature sensor or control board is misreading. This is more likely if F2 comes back with light use. What to do:
1. Switch the hob off and let it cool fully for 20 to 30 minutes. If F2 doesn't clear, turn it off at the wall isolator or breaker for a few minutes, then back on. If it clears and works normally, it was very likely just a thermal cut-out.
2. Check what's underneath. Clear anything packed against the underside, such as a drawer full of pans or tea towels, and make sure nothing blocks the air gaps. If an oven sits below, avoid running both flat out together for long periods.
3. Next time it's on, listen for the fan. It's usually a faint whirr from under the hob once a zone is running, and it often carries on for a while after you switch off. If you never hear it, the fan may not be working.
4. Keep hot pans off the touch-control strip and centred on their zones, as heat near the controls can add to the problem. If F2 keeps coming back with only one or two zones on at moderate settings, or the fan seems silent, that points to the cooling fan or a sensor/control fault. That needs an engineer, as it means removing the hob from the worktop and working on mains-connected electronics. To help narrow it down: is there an oven or a drawer directly under the hob, and was the oven on at the same time?

There's a cutlery drawer directly under the hob, no oven under it. It's stuffed full with tea towels pressed right up against the underside. The oven wasn't on. Once I let it cool for about 15 minutes F2 cleared and it worked again. The fan was running loudly too. It only happens when I've had all four on high for about 40 minutes, normal cooking is fine.

That all points one way, and it's good news. F2 cleared after cooling, the fan was clearly working, and it only happens after about 40 minutes with all four zones on high. That's the hob's overheating protection doing its job, not a fault. The tea towels pressed right up against the underside will have been making it worse. Induction electronics need to pull in and push out air underneath, and packed fabric chokes that airflow, so the fan can't keep up under full load. The one tip that should stop it: clear the tea towels out of that drawer, or at least keep a few centimetres of space between the contents and the underside of the hob. Cutlery in a tray is fine. Soft stuff packed to the top isn't. For long batch cooks, it also helps to drop one or two rings to a medium setting once things are up to temperature, rather than running all four flat out. If F2 ever starts appearing with only one or two zones on at normal settings, even with the drawer cleared, that would point to a cooling or sensor problem worth getting an engineer to look at. Is there anything else I can help with?

candidates: Overheat protection from heavy use (all four zones at high power for a long time) (high)
Poor ventilation under the hob (blocked air path, items stored underneath, oven below running) (medium)
Cooling fan not running properly, or a temperature sensor/control fault (low)

reading.symptom: one zone switched off with F2 code

plan: They asked: "What does F2 mean?" - answer that first.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Bosch; model PIE631BB5E; code F2.
The fault they reported is: "one zone switched off with F2 code". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.
